title: Quantitative X-ray Mapping of Ni Superalloys
content: Development of Ni superalloys are key to improving high-performance engine components. However, the characterization of compositional variations in their constituent phases is can be difficult due to the small size of the phases, the presence of light elements such as boron, carbon and oxygen, and fine microstructures that are found in the material [1,2]. This paper describes the characterization of two Ni-alloy samples via wavelength-dispersive X-ray spectrometry, and the challenges inherent therein, particularly regarding measurements of the first-row transition metals (22 ≤ Z ≤ 30) in these alloys.
